messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: log-alert 'api-error-rate' is firing in prod (alert_id=LA-9087). 3500 hits in the last 2m, threshold 2000. Severity: P2.

maya: seeing the same in SLO channel. Error pattern looks like transient downstream timeouts from the routing layer. Paging oncall now.

jon: i'm on it, grabbing the on-call box. ETA 2m. Any customer impact?

sam: partial degradations on streaming endpoints reported by three customers. Not full outage but increased latencies and 5xxs.

maya: tagging @jon for mitigation; @lee for logs / alert changes.

jon: diving into logs. First glance: lots of errors with message "upstream connection reset" and a bunch of hits from internal healthcheck agent hitting /api/v1/generate?hc=1

lee: thanks — that matches what I saw in the query results. Healthchecks from the load-tester were misconfigured, basically hitting the heavy path and spiking token work. We should temporarily mute noisy rule and add an exclusion for healthcheck path.

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident created: INC-2026-04-11-regen-spike. Runbook: https://internal.redwood/ops/runbooks/api-error-rate

jon: mitigation plan: 1) Mute paging for 'api-error-rate' for 15m while we add regex exclusion. 2) Add LogQL filter excluding path "/healthz" and queries from load-tester agent. 3) Roll threshold up slightly while we verify. 4) Monitor customer errors.

maya: agree. I'll notify customer-facing teams and keep comms short.

lee: prepping the LogQL tweak. Proposed snippet:
```
{job="redwood-api"} |= "upstream connection reset" | regexp -s "(?i)^(?!.*(\/healthz|load-tester-agent)).*$"
```
This will keep the core signature but exclude lines with /healthz or load-tester-agent.

sam: can we instead use a negative match on labels? e.g., `| label:not(name="load-tester")` — our exporters attach `agent=load-tester` label. Safer than regex?

lee: good point. i'll do both: label exclude and query regex. New combined rule:
```
{job="redwood-api", agent!="load-tester"} |= "upstream connection reset" |~ "(?i)^(?!.*\/healthz).*"
```
Applying now.

incident-bot: :hourglass_flowing_sand: Mute request submitted for alert LA-9087 (15m) by lee.

jon: rolled the mute, and applied the LogQL change. Observing metrics...

maya: customer comms: posted initial note to #customer-status: "We observed elevated error rates on streaming API due to misdirected healthchecks; mitigation in progress. No data loss reported; reducing noise for on-call. Follow-up will include long term alert refinement." :loudspeaker:

sam: looks quieter. 5xx rate dropped to baseline in the last 90s. Paging noise down.

jon: removing temp threshold bump. Keeping mute for remaining 10m to avoid flapping.

lee: filing follow-up tasks: 1) tighten alert to use `agent` label exclusions and path checks (done), 2) create a dashboard panel showing agent label distribution for error spikes, 3) add unit test that simulates load-tester traffic so future changes don't re-enable noise, 4) add regex signature for "connection reset" + worker id pattern to reduce false positives. I'll attach PR.

maya: thx. Also suggest adding a lightweight KPI in alert description indicating expected noise floor and links to the new dashboard. Helps future oncalls.

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: INC-2026-04-11-regen-spike marked as mitigated by jon. Mute will expire in 10m.

jon: handing off to @lee for postmortem & cleanup. I'm done for this rotation.

lee: taking handoff. I'll open a post-incident postmortem and include the LogQL diffs and PR link. Preliminary root cause: misconfigured load-tester healthcheck hitting heavy generation path. Action items assigned.

maya: thanks team. Good quick mitigation. Follow-up owners: lee (postmortem + alert rule update), sam (dashboard), jon (verification + runbook update). I'll lock to ensure no further page noise. :lock:

incident-bot: :information_source: Next steps checklist: create dashboard (#incidents-dashboard), PR with rule change (link forthcoming), schedule 1hr review with devex to ensure load-test configs are correct."
